To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We provide a methodology for closed loop, humanlike, reaching and grasping of objects with redundant robot arms using human demonstrations.
We propose a methodology for humanlike, task specific robot motion and grasping, that is capable to guarantee robustness and convergence to the desired goal.
We propose a novel methodology for humanlike, task specific reaching and grasping, that involves redundant robot arms and simple robot hands.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel methodology that provides humanlike, taskspecific robot motion, task compatibility indexes, robust and task-specific grasps and guaranteed convergence to desired goals, for a robot arm hand system.
the development of a methodology that provides anthropomorphic robot motions, task-specific robot configurations and robust grasps, in a closed-loop fashion.
the following issues: (1) Humanlike reaching and grasping motion generation, (2) Task-specific reaching and graspping motion generation, and (3) Task-specific grasping postures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed scheme is a novel methodology that provides human-like, task-specific reaching, grasping and manipulation with redundant arms and robot hands.
the proposed scheme provides humanlike robot arm motion and hand grasps, task-specific robot configurations and robust grasps, optimized fingertips placement and guaranteed convergence to goals.
the proposed scheme provides anthropomorphic, robust and task-specific motion for robot arms and hands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a methodology to achieve task-specific reaching and humanlike grasping for redundant robot arms and hands.

we have proposed a novel methodology for humanlike, task specific reaching and grasping of objects, that is based on human demonstrations, and can be used with redundant robot arms, low-complexity hand systems and a-priori unknown object positions.
a humanlike robot arm can perform task-specific reaching and grasp motions in a robust and efficient way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a robot hand with low degrees of freedom can be used to perform humanlike, task specific reaching and grasping tasks.
a robot arm hand system with a low-complexity hand can perform humanlike, task specific reaching and grasping tasks, if appropriate humanlike robot motion is provided and robust grasps are computed.
the proposed methods can be used for the generation of humanlike, task specific reaching and grasping motion, with low-complexity, humanlike robot hands, for different objects and tasks.
